Before Anthony Bourdain became a bestselling author, television icon, and one of the world’s most recognizable chefs, he was a troubled 19-year-old trying to figure out what to do with his life.⁣
⁣
Matt Johnson’s 𝐓𝐎𝐍𝐘 (𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟔) takes a different approach to the traditional biopic. Rather than covering Bourdain’s rise to fame, the film focuses on one summer in 1975, when a failed attempt to pursue writing leads him to Provincetown, Massachusetts. There, he unexpectedly finds himself working in a restaurant kitchen, discovering a world that would shape the rest of his life.⁣
⁣
Dominic Sessa (The Holdovers) plays the young Bourdain, capturing his arrogance, insecurity, and self-destructive tendencies without attempting a direct impersonation. Shot on 16mm, the film recreates the atmosphere of the 1970s, particularly during its hectic kitchen sequences. Johnson avoids romanticizing Bourdain, instead portraying a selfish, often difficult young man who gradually discovers a sense of belonging through food and the people around him.⁣
⁣
Knowing what Bourdain would eventually accomplish, and how his life tragically ended in 2018, gives this early chapter an added emotional weight. TONY isn’t about the legend Anthony Bourdain became. It’s about the young man who had no idea what was waiting for him.⁣
⁣
